$comment: The enforced gate on ambiguous watermarks (SPEC.md §7, issue #16).
tvtracker recorded most watches per episode, but a few titles carry watches only as
shows.watched_through — an absolute ordinal across the whole show, with no record of
which episodes it counted. Where that ordinal claims more watches than the episode rows
account for, and the show was not watched right through, the export simply does not say
which episodes those were. The conversion halts and names them rather than guess.
This file is where a person answers, and it is deliberately EMPTY. Two shows in the
2026-08-16 export need an answer nobody has given yet:
Hudson & Rex (tmdb 87940) — watched through 60 of 122; 53 episodes marked watched,
leaving 7 unaccounted for. The named episodes have real gaps (S1E1-10, S2E8-11)
that contradict a watermark of 60, so 'the first 60' is not a safe reading.
Person of Interest (tmdb 1411) — watched through 7 of 103, with no episode rows at
all. There is no evidence in either direction.
To answer one, add an entry naming the episodes to credit:
{ "tmdb_id": 1411, "title": "Person of Interest",
"reason": "why this is the right answer",
"credit": [ { "season": 1, "episode": 1 } ] }
`credit` is an explicit list, never a count — a count would put the guess back in the
script. An EMPTY `credit` is a real answer too: it records that the watermark is stale
and that nothing should be written for that show.
tvtracker is re-exported at cutover, so this file is not a checklist that was ticked
once. A fresh export with different stragglers halts on them, and an answer left here
for a show that no longer needs one halts too, rather than being inherited unread.
